Hannah — following up with the materials we discussed. Summary below, and I attached the two files: a draft attestation template and the current subprocessor inventory.

Summary answers (short):
- No-training assurance: Redwood offers an opt-out/no-training mode for tenant traffic. When enabled for a tenant we: disable dataset retention for model training, disable routing to experimental training pipelines, and treat interactions as non-consumptive for model improvement. We will provide a signed attestation on Redwood letterhead for MedSys (attached).

- Subprocessor inventory: Attached CSV lists each subprocessor, primary function, hosting region, and processing location. High level: most infra subprocessors are in US/EU (AWS, GCS partners); inference runtime hosts used for dedicated customers can be restricted to specific regions for enterprise/private deployments. See CSV for host countries.

- Geo-routing & KMS residency: For EU-origin traffic we support EU-region routing for both inference and key management for Dedicated/Private tiers. For hosted tenants we offer onshore KMS and IP routing options per contract (we can pin to a region with an SLA). We documented the routing approach in the Drive link below.

- Operational evidence we can share:
  * Signed no-training attestation (PDF) — attached as "no_train_attestation_medical_template.pdf" (please review if legal wants different wording).
  * Subprocessor inventory CSV — attached as "subprocessors_inventory_2026-06.csv".
  * Network/residency overview (internal Drive): shows how requests are routed and where KV persistence is stored; we can export sanitized logs for SLA auditing under an NDA if required.

Technical clarifications worth noting:
- Ephemeral KV and prefix caching: tenant requests can be set to ephemeral-only storage; we record traces for monitoring but those traces are excluded from model improvement when no-training is enabled.
- Exports & escrow: For customers who require independent verification we support on-prem SFTP exports of interaction logs (redacted) and can provide signed snapshots under the DPA addendum.
